The 3-minute quiz lets you compare your pay, hours, benefits, and more.Take The Breakroom QuizAs of Apr 16, 2026, the average annual pay for a Nasa Astronaut in the United States is $49,837 a year.Just in case you need a simple salary calculator, that works out to be approximately $23.96 an hour. This is the equivalent of $958/week or $4,153/month.While ZipRecruiter is seeing annual salaries as high as $70,000 and as low as $31,000, the majority of Nasa Astronaut salaries currently range between $42,000 (25th percentile) to $55,000 (75th percentile) with top earners (90th percentile) making $63,000 annually across the United States. The average pay range for a Nasa Astronaut varies greatly (by as much as 13000), which suggests there may be many opportunities for advancement and increased pay based on skill level, location and years of experience.A Nasa Astronaut in your area makes on average $48,452 per year, or $1,385 (2.779%) less than the national average annual salary of $49,837. Missouri ranks number 45 out of 50 states nationwide for Nasa Astronaut salaries.To estimate the most accurate annual salary range for Nasa Astronaut jobs, ZipRecruiter continuously scans its database of millions of active jobs published locally throughout America.Find your next high paying job as a Nasa Astronaut on ZipRecruiter today.We've identified 10 cities where the typical salary for a Nasa Astronaut job is above the national average. Topping the list is Kentville, NS, , with Carcross, YT, and Haines Junction, YT, close behind in the second and third positions. Haines Junction, YT, beats the national average by $51,799 (103.9%), and Kentville, NS, furthers that trend with another $52,860 (106.1%) above the $49,837 average.With these 10 cities having average salaries higher than the national average, the opportunities for economic advancement by changing locations as a Nasa Astronaut appears to be exceedingly fruitful.Finally, another factor to consider is the average salary for these top 10 cities varies very little at 4% between Kentville, NS, and Saint John, NB, , reinforcing the limited potential for much wage advancement.
